new_statements.quote: En outre, l’écoute d’enregistrements de sillanka (une variante du soninké parlée au Burkina Faso) réalisés par Anna Marie Diagne montre que, dans la mesure où les mots soninké n’ont pas été remplacés en sillanka par des mots empruntés à une autre langue, les phrases de ce parler (qui géographiquement est complètement coupé du reste du domaine soninké) ont des mélodies tonales très semblables à celles des phrases correspondantes dans les parlers du Kingi, du Diafounou ou de Kaédi. [p. 76:] il a introduit des notions (ton moyen, accent) qui ne sont pas pertinentes pour décrire le système tonal soninké
new_statements.translation: Moreover, listening to recordings of Sillanka (a variety of Soninke spoken in Burkina Faso) made by Anna Marie Diagne shows that, insofar as the Soninke words have not been replaced in Sillanka by words borrowed from another language, the sentences of this variety (which is geographically completely cut off from the rest of the Soninke domain) have tonal melodies very similar to those of the corresponding sentences in the Kingi, Diafounou or Kaédi varieties. [p. 76:] he [O. M. Diagana] introduced notions (mid tone, accent) that are not pertinent for describing the Soninke tonal system
new_statements.citation: Creissels, Denis. 2016. Phonologie segmentale et tonale du soninké (parler du Kingi). Mandenkan 55: 3-174.
new_statements.locator: §3.1 Remarques préliminaires, pp. 27-28 (Sillanka passage); §4 Conclusion, p. 76 (accent not a pertinent notion for the Soninke tonal system)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: (172 pp., text layer; page-1 header 'Mandenkan 55, 2016, pp. 3-174', title 'Phonologie segmentale et tonale du soninké (parler du Kingi)'). The Sillanka sentence is verbatim in §3.1 Remarques préliminaires, pp. 27-28 (the text layer; page break after 'complètement coupé'), and 'il a introduit des notions (ton moyen, accent) qui ne sont pas pertinentes pour décrire le système tonal soninké' is verbatim in §4 Conclusion, p. 76 (the text layer). Surrounding section read: Creissels describes Kingi Soninke as a two-tone (H/B) system, TBU = syllable, marked-L; Sillanka is said, on Diagne's recordings, to have tonal melodies 'très semblables' to Kingi/Diafounou/Kaédi insofar as Soninke words have…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for sini1242; this is the first sourced statement: the language is tonal (Soninke-type H/L tone, melodies like eastern Soninke), with no word-stress statement. The work as a whole describes Kingi Soninke (Mali), not Sillanka; only the pp. 27-28 passage is about Sillanka.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sillanka (= Sininkere) is a tonal Soninke variety: on Diagne's recordings its sentences carry tonal melodies very similar to those of the eastern Soninke varieties (Kingi, Diafounou, Kaédi), whose system Creissels describes as a two-tone (H/L) system with the syllable as tone-bearing unit and marked L tone, and for which he says the notion of 'accent' is not pertinent. No word-stress rule is stated for Sillanka or for Soninke.
new_statements.exceptions: The Sillanka statement is hedged: it holds 'insofar as the Soninke words have not been replaced in Sillanka by loanwords from another language', and rests on listening to recordings, not on a description of Sillanka itself. Separately (p. 6 and p. 28) Creissels says Bakel Soninke (Senegal) shows very different prosodic realisations and may be losing its tone system; that concerns Bakel, not Sillanka.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog sini1242 'Sininkere' (ISO skq, Burkina Faso; alt. names Silanke, Silinkere) is the variety Creissels and Diagne call Sillanka, a geographically isolated Soninke dialect (Glottolog classifies it under Soninke/Soninkean; the HAL abstract calls it 'a highly distinctive Soninke dialect and linguistic island spoken in central-western Burkina Faso'). Creissels 2016 describes the Kingi variety of Soninke (Nioro, north-west Mali), with first-hand data also from Diafounou and Kaédi; the Sillanka statement (pp. 27-28) is based on recordings made by Anna Marie Diagne. The remark on Bakel Soninke possibly losing tone concerns Senegal, not Sillanka.
